gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ALLPOWERS sells the same P1800 (1,024 Wh, up to 650 W solar input) with a 600 W panel for $798 on its US store. That kit has 50% more panel than ChatGPT's $698 pick (P1800 + 400 W) for $100 more, which works out to about 2.6 peak-sun hours to full instead of about 3.9.
standout_why: I opened two of the results. Trek4Tech (cited, updated 2026-11-09) covers only 200–400 W bundles, with estimates of 5.4–8.9 peak-sun hours, and gives no prices. RuntimeMath (2026-11-11) puts its fastest pairing at an ALLPOWERS R1500 plus a 600 W SP039 bought separately ($938, 2.7 sun hours). That is not a bundle, and the page does not list the P1800 600 W kit. I could not read TheOutagePlan, the other cited page, because the fetch failed with a self-signed certificate error. ChatGPT's own cards stop at 400 W of panel per 1,024 Wh. Our page (dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included) may already list the P1800 600 W kit, since it is in our catalog as allpowers-p1800-600w-solar-kit, but ChatGPT did not cite it.
decides: ChatGPT ranked kits by panel watts per battery Wh. On that same measure the P1800 + 600 W kit beats every card it showed: 0.59 W per Wh against 0.39 for all three cards. It is also $434 cheaper than BLUETTI's 400 W AC180 kit. That makes it the fastest-refilling kit I could price today. The P1800 + 400 W stays the value pick. I also found that the EcoFlow 400 W panel in ChatGPT's DELTA 3 Plus card shows as sold out on EcoFlow's US store, so that card's bundle may not be buyable there right now. A DJI Power 1000 + 4 × 200 W bundle exists and could be faster, but I could not get its price or input limit.
